actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/git.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/git.purpose: Inspect or change Git repository state.

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@cli/shell.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/shell.note: Resolve to the session shell (PowerShell, bash or another declared shell); do not assume bash on Windows. Arguments remain separate data until encoded for that shell.
@cli/shell.purpose: Run a declared command in the active session shell.

@tools/fileread.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.

@workspaces/skills.purpose: The explicitly bound skill runtime directory.

Evidence and manifest files match their digests.

onFail.instruction: Ask for the missing or changed evidence.

items.expect: The response satisfies the knowledge repair contract.
The response binds this request revision.
Artifact files are scoped and digest-correct.

onFail.instruction: Re-read bytes and repair the artifact or metadata.

items.expect: Observations reference declared criteria and evidence.
Concrete evidence applies to the challenged rule and case.

onFail.instruction: Name the evidence gap and ask for a directly applicable observation.

items.expect: The smallest canonical owner contains the complete repair.

onFail.instruction: Remove duplicated or unrelated edits and repair the one owner.

items.expect: Published identifiers and thresholds remain stable.

onFail.instruction: Restore stable addresses and append cases or retire explicitly.

items.expect: The result binds a fresh rerun on the same originating surface.

onFail.instruction: Correct manifest and rerun references without claiming acceptance.

onFail.instruction: Return blocked with the exact missing capability.

items.expect: Challenge, canonical owner, manifest, evidence and rerun target are supplied.

onFail.instruction: Ask for the missing evidence or binding.

onFail.instruction: Inspect current knowledge and Git state, then retry only the incomplete validation.

criteria.stopWhen: Return done only when every criterion and criteriaResults entry passes; then require the originating operation to reevaluate the same surface. Stop after two feedback rounds or an unchanged repeated failure.

purpose: Repair one challenged knowledge rule at its canonical owner from concrete evidence, preserve stable identifiers, and publish an exact post-repair manifest for reevaluation.

request.description: inputs.prompts identify one challenged rule, its canonical owner, originating operation and same surface/reference for reevaluation. inputs.files carry concrete contradictory evidence and the exact pre-repair manifest. context files may include the consumer observation but cannot replace direct evidence.
request.title: knowledge.repair request

response.description: A done response identifies one bounded knowledge commit, evidence-based repair report and exact post-repair manifest. The originating operation must still reevaluate the same surface.
response.title: knowledge.repair response

scope: One canonical knowledge file and directly required language mirror or manifest metadata. It does not patch consumers, edit generated output, change routing or aliases, publish a UI package, or declare the repaired rule visually correct.

calls.purpose: Read the exact challenged authority, manifest and concrete evidence.

steps.instruction: Read the challenged rule, exact pre-repair manifest, originating surface/reference and concrete evidence. Confirm applicability and identify one canonical owner before writing. Ask for missing evidence; reject a request that belongs to a consumer fix.
produces: A validated challenge and canonical owner.

reads.when: for each evidence or manifest file

calls.purpose: Apply the smallest canonical evidence-backed repair.

steps.instruction: Answer the maintenance questions in order: enforce an existing rule first, add a concept only when it has no home, correct a too-narrow rule in place, and fold duplicate homes. Edit only the canonical authority and directly required mirror while preserving stable identifiers and thresholds.

writes.when: when the knowledge set requires a language mirror

calls.purpose: Run only the declared manifest and knowledge validation commands.
Persist manifest, report and targeted repair metadata.

steps.instruction: Rebuild the exact manifest, compare all stable ids and changed concepts, and inspect the diff for duplicated authority or unrelated edits. Write the repair report with evidence links and an explicit fresh-rerun binding; repair only the failed owner detail and reassess.

calls.purpose: Commit the exact canonical owner repair once.
Validate the compiled request and response.

steps.instruction: Create one local knowledge commit, re-read its tree and validate the response. Return done only after all criteria pass; the response directs the originating operation to rerun on the same surface and makes no acceptance claim.

validate.failurePolicy: Inspect evidence, repair the smallest canonical owner, rebuild the manifest and reassess. Concrete feedback returns to evidence selection or the owner edit. An unchanged repeated challenge stops rather than rewriting the rule again.

review.instruction: Verify the concrete evidence actually contradicts the challenged rule in its declared case and comes from the same relevant surface or family. A consumer preference or single unexplained mismatch is insufficient.

Confirm the repair occurs in the one canonical owner and chooses correction of an existing rule before adding a concept. Reject duplicated thresholds, consumer patches, generated-file edits and unrelated cleanup.
Compare before and after authority. Existing rule identifiers retain their address and meaning unless explicitly retired to a named survivor; new cases append without renumbering.

Require the post-repair manifest and response to name the originating operation, exact surface/reference and current owner bytes for a fresh rerun. The repair itself cannot claim visual or behavioral acceptance.
